t: This is the equestrian statue of Richard the Lionheart, standing on a granite pedestal in Old Palace Yard, outside the Palace of Westminster. Richard was King of England from 1189 to 1199, and he wasn't expected to inherit the throne, because he was the third of five sons. The sculptor was Baron Carlo Marochetti, an Italian-born artist who settled in England in 1848 and worked for Queen Victoria. The statue was first shown in clay at the Great Exhibition in 1851. Two years later, Victoria and Prince Albert led the subscribers raising money to cast it in bronze. It is Grade II listed.
